Pula Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pula, Croatia

Not demolished. Pula's Jewish community dates to the 14th century, drawn mainly from Germany and engaged in banking and business; the town's first Jewish bank was organized in 1427. Jewish burials took place across two municipal cemeteries — Cemetery Monte Ghiro, which had a separate section for non-Catholics, and the K.u.K. Marinefriedhof, the Austro-Hungarian Naval Cemetery — though neither saw further use after WWI. Economic crises drove many Jews from the town over time, leaving only 112 by 1900. Today, 42 tombstones survive across both former burial sites, ranging from 1892 to 1918.
